historicalInsight.stringValue: Early Filipino communities depended on different livelihood activities such as farming, fishing, and crafts.

exploreIntroduction.stringValue: Look around the barangay! Different people are working to provide food and useful goods for their community. Explore each activity to discover how early Filipinos made a living.

values.stringValue: farming
fishing

keyTermDefinition.stringValue: Livelihood refers to the work and activities people do to provide for their needs and support their families. In early Filipino communities, livelihoods included farming, fishing, making crafts, and trading goods.

discoveryText.stringValue: Early Filipino communities relied on different livelihood activities to meet their needs. Farming, fishing, and crafting helped provide food, tools, and useful goods. The activities of each community depended partly on its environment, available resources, and the skills of its people.

imageCaption.stringValue: Early Filipinos practiced different livelihoods, including farming, fishing, and crafting, depending on their environment, resources, and skills.

content.stringValue: As you explore the community, you see people working to provide food and other needs for their families. Farming, fishing, and making useful goods are important parts of everyday life.

discovery.stringValue: In many early Filipino communities, people cultivated crops such as rice and root crops. Farming provided food and was shaped by local land, water, and environmental conditions.

hint.stringValue: Discover how people gathered food from the water.

discovery.stringValue: Communities near rivers, lakes, and seas could depend on fishing and other aquatic resources. People used knowledge of their environment and different fishing methods to help provide food.

hint.stringValue: See how people made useful objects.

discovery.stringValue: Skilled community members created useful products from available materials, including pottery, woven goods, and tools. These products supported daily activities and could also be exchanged through trade.

discoveryTitle.stringValue: How Early Filipinos Made a Living

imageAlt.stringValue: Storybook illustration showing farming, fishing, pottery, and weaving as livelihood activities in an early Philippine community.

historicalInsight.stringValue: The natural resources available to communities influenced the kinds of livelihood activities people practiced.

checkExplanation.stringValue: Communities used the natural resources available around them to produce food, tools, crafts, and other useful goods.

discoveryText.stringValue: The environment influenced how early Filipino communities made a living. People in areas with suitable farmland could grow crops, while communities near rivers and seas could obtain food through fishing. Natural materials such as bamboo, wood, clay, and plant fibers also helped people create useful products. Livelihood activities varied depending on local resources, skills, and surroundings.

hint.stringValue: Explore how people used the land to grow food.

discovery.stringValue: In communities with suitable land and water, early Filipinos cultivated crops such as rice and root crops. Farming methods varied according to the local environment and available resources.

hint.stringValue: Discover how nearby waters provided food.

discovery.stringValue: Communities near rivers, lakes, and coastal waters could obtain fish and other aquatic resources. People developed fishing methods suited to their surroundings and used their knowledge of local waters.

hint.stringValue: Investigate how people used nearby materials.

discovery.stringValue: Early Filipinos used locally available materials such as bamboo, wood, clay, and plant fibers to create useful objects. The materials found in an area influenced the products people could make.

content.stringValue: You notice community members producing and gathering different goods. Some grow crops, others catch fish, while skilled workers create useful items from materials available around them.

imageCaption.stringValue: Early Filipino communities used resources from their surroundings to produce food and useful goods.

values.stringValue: farming
fishing

historicalInsight.stringValue: Trade allowed early Filipino communities to exchange products and obtain resources from other places.

values.stringValue: It allowed communities to exchange goods and obtain things they needed
It stopped communities from producing their own goods

imageCaption.stringValue: Trade connected early Philippine communities and helped people obtain goods from other places.

hint.stringValue: Discover what people brought to exchange.

discovery.stringValue: Early Filipino communities could exchange products such as crops, woven goods, pottery, and other locally made items. The goods available for trade depended on the resources and skills of each community.

hint.stringValue: Find out why people traveled to exchange goods.

discovery.stringValue: People traveled between communities to exchange products. Trade also connected some early Filipino communities with merchants from other parts of Asia, allowing goods, ideas, and cultural influences to move between places.

Not every community produced the same goods. Through trade, people could obtain useful products that were less available in their own area. Exchanges depended on the needs, resources, and relationships of the people involved.

content.stringValue: Near the shore, you see people exchanging goods with visitors from other communities. Products they have in abundance can be traded for things that are harder to obtain locally.

checkExplanation.stringValue: Trade connected communities and allowed people to exchange their products for other goods they needed.

barter-exchange

exploreIntroduction.stringValue: You arrive at a busy trading place near the shore. People from different communities are exchanging useful goods. Explore what they brought and discover why trade was important to early Filipino communities.

checkQuestion.stringValue: How did trade help early Filipino communities?

discoveryText.stringValue: Early Filipino communities exchanged goods to obtain products they needed or valued. They traded locally produced items such as crops, pottery, and woven goods. Trade connected different communities and, in some areas, brought people into contact with merchants from other parts of Asia. These exchanges helped support livelihoods and encouraged the sharing of goods, knowledge, and ideas.

hint.stringValue: Discover how clay became useful containers.

discovery.stringValue: Early Filipino potters shaped clay into containers used for cooking, storing food, and other daily activities. Pottery required knowledge of materials, shaping techniques, and firing.

hint.stringValue: Explore how plants became useful woven goods.

discovery.stringValue: People in different communities used plant fibers and other suitable materials to weave baskets, mats, and other useful products. Weaving required skill and knowledge passed through generations.

hint.stringValue: Investigate how materials became everyday tools.

discovery.stringValue: Early Filipinos made tools using materials such as wood, stone, and metal, depending on local resources and available technology. These tools supported activities including farming, fishing, and other work.

values.stringValue: Shape and fire clay into a suitable storage pot.
Leave the grains on the ground without a container.
Stop making useful objects because natural materials cannot be used.
Throw away the available materials instead of using them.

exploreIntroduction.stringValue: You enter a busy crafting area where skilled community members are making useful objects. Explore three activities to discover how early Filipinos transformed natural materials into everyday products.

content.stringValue:
As you continue exploring the community, you hear the sounds of people working with different materials. Nearby, someone shapes clay into a pot, while others weave plant fibers into useful containers and prepare tools for daily activities.
You discover that making these objects requires knowledge, practice, and skill. People use materials available in their surroundings to create products that help their families and communities.
Some of these useful goods can also be exchanged with other communities.

decisionCorrectAnswer.stringValue: Shape and fire clay into a suitable storage pot.

decisionExplanation.stringValue: Early Filipino craftspeople used their knowledge and skills to turn natural materials into useful products. A properly made clay pot could help a family store harvested food. This shows how craftsmanship supported everyday needs and livelihoods.

imageAlt.stringValue: Storybook illustration of early Philippine craftspeople shaping clay pots, weaving baskets from plant fibers, and making useful tools in a sheltered workshop.

keyTermDefinition.stringValue: Craftsmanship is the skill of making useful or decorative objects by hand. In early Filipino communities, skilled people made pottery, woven goods, tools, and other products using materials available in their surroundings.

decisionSituation.stringValue: A family in an early Filipino community needs a container to store harvested grains. A skilled craftsperson has access to clay, bamboo, and plant fibers. The family asks for a sturdy container that can help protect their stored food.

discoveryTitle.stringValue: How Craft Skills Supported Daily Life

values.stringValue: craftsmanship

imageCaption.stringValue: Skilled craftspeople transformed clay, plant fibers, wood, and other materials into useful objects for everyday life.

discoveryText.stringValue: Early Filipino communities developed skills to turn natural materials into useful products. Pottery provided containers for cooking and storage, weaving produced baskets and mats, and toolmaking supported work such as farming and fishing. These crafts helped meet everyday needs, and some finished products could also be exchanged through trade.

historicalInsight.stringValue: Early Filipino communities developed different craft skills, including pottery, weaving, and toolmaking. These skills helped people transform natural materials into useful products. Craft traditions and available materials varied across communities.

content.stringValue:
Before leaving the community, you meet several families preparing for their daily activities. Some are gathering food, others are making useful objects, and a group of traders is preparing to exchange goods with a nearby community.
A community elder invites you to think about what you have discovered. How can people use their surroundings, skills, and available products to meet different needs?
You prepare to apply what you have learned about farming, fishing, natural resources, crafts, and trade.

historicalInsight.stringValue: Early Filipino communities used their knowledge of the environment, natural resources, and practical skills to support their livelihoods. Farming, fishing, crafts, and trade helped people meet everyday needs. These activities varied according to each community's location and resources.

values.stringValue: farming

Coastal communities could obtain fish, while other communities cultivated crops or made useful products. Through trade, communities could exchange goods and obtain things they needed.

content.stringValue:
Bayani brings you to the final investigation. Your community has extra grain but needs pots for storing food. Visitors have pots and need grain.

In this made-up exchange, the two groups agree to swap 3 baskets of grain for 2 pots. This agreement is part of the classroom activity. It is not a fixed price used by all early communities.

First inspect what each group has and needs. Record the clues in your evidence journal. Then choose what to offer and what to receive. Check whether both needs are met and whether the plan follows the agreement.

After checking your plan, explain why it helps both communities. No real goods or game XP are spent in this activity.

values.stringValue: Each community gives a good the other needs and receives a useful good.
Only the community receiving grain can benefit.
Trade makes both communities have exactly the same resources.
After one exchange, neither community will need to produce goods again.

hint.stringValue: What do we have, and what do we need?

discovery.stringValue: We have 8 baskets of grain and 3 woven baskets available for exchange. We need 2 pots for storing food.

hint.stringValue: What can the visitors offer, and what do they need?

discovery.stringValue: The visitors have 4 pots and 2 mats available. They need 3 baskets of grain.

hint.stringValue: What exchange have both groups agreed on?

discovery.stringValue: For this made-up activity, both groups agree on 3 baskets of grain for 2 pots. Trading another good or changing just one side does not follow this agreement. These quantities are not a historical price list.

values.stringValue: Our supplies: 8 baskets of grain and 3 woven baskets. Our need: 2 pots.
Visitors' supplies: 4 pots and 2 mats. Their need: 3 baskets of grain.
Activity agreement: 3 baskets of grain for 2 pots. This is a fictional learning agreement, not a historical price.

instructions.stringValue: Use your evidence journal. Choose the good and amount we offer, then the good and amount we receive. Check both communities' needs and the agreed exchange.

title.stringValue: Plan an Exchange That Helps Both Sides

decisionExplanation.stringValue: Our community receives pots for storing food. The visitors receive grain they need. Different resources and skills can connect communities through trade. The quantities in this activity do not describe every historical exchange.

explanation.stringValue: An exchange can help both groups when each receives something it needs. Count the goods, check the agreement, and then explain the benefit. A plan can fail because of the wrong good, too few goods, too many goods, or an exchange that does not match the agreement.

definition.stringValue: Exchanging goods or services directly without money.
A plan that the people involved accept.

example.stringValue: If one group needs a storage container and another needs food, compare the goods each group can offer.

guidingQuestion.stringValue: What does each group still need? Does your plan meet both needs without using more goods than either group has?

decisionCorrectAnswer.stringValue: Each community gives a good the other needs and receives a useful good.

introduction.stringValue:
Travel back to the Philippines before Spanish colonization and discover how early Filipino communities made a living.
Explore farms, fishing areas, workshops, and trading places. Investigate how people used natural resources, developed useful skills, and exchanged goods to support their families and communities.
Follow historical clues, make thoughtful decisions, and prepare for your Mission Trial.

learningObjective.stringValue: Explain how farming, fishing, crafts, natural resources, and trade supported the livelihood and economic activities of early Filipino communities.

lessonRecap.stringValue: Farming, fishing and craft skills helped communities use local resources for daily needs. Trade connected communities with different products and resources.
